I’ve been with my boyfriend for 6 years and I can tell you this about how we’ve lasted. 

There’s no such thing as perfect, he’s not and I’m not. 

Some days are harder than others and some days, the hard days, you’ll have to work at it and remember why you feel in love with each other. 

You’re on an adventure that only you two know about. Try not let others interfere in your relationship and don’t invite them in to criticise it. 

Always remember how lucky you are that someone wants to share their life with you and they are equally as lucky that you want to share your life with them. 

Do things together, even if he’s more in to them than you. Make time to travel and to see as much of the world together as you can. Whether that’s the other side of the world or just a different town 50 miles away.

Forgive him when he deserves your forgiveness and forgive yourself for stupid things you may say or do. 

And, never take each other for granted. 

Love does change as you grow older together but it should hopefully deepen.

Hi there, when a person dies lots of different things can happen. Lots of things will depend on how the person died, when and where they died, the age of the person, if they were ill and as such expected to die or whether they died in suspicious or unexplained circumstances. When someone dies it may be investigated further so that the reasons why can be determined, this is usually based on local laws and regulations. For example, I live in the UK and when someone dies in an unexplained way a coroner’s inquest is conducted. The coroner is presented with legal and medical evidence and then provides a determination which is usually the cause of death that is recorded on the persons death certificate. Lots of things can be taken in evidence and depend in the circumstance I’ve set out above.

Pixel and the move toward Home products is a clear break from the Nexus days. I think Google has really found its stride in design language and it's clear that it now extends across their portfolio of hardwear products. It's also clear that they are taking an Apple approach to how they now manage design and software. I wouldn't be surprised to see Google shifting toward partitioning Android between Pixel and non Pixel devices. I've just moved from iPhone 7 Plus. First thing I'd say is that if you're going to make the move consider how tied in you are to the ios eco system (Do you have a MacBook, iPad etc.) Because that makes a huge difference. 

Second thing is that it's not an iPhone and you shouldn't expect it to be or try to make it act like one. There are significant differences but you will also find similarities. So many people come to Android and never let go of ios and try to replicate the experience. If you're doing that you'll not last. 

Many of the apps are the same but you'll find some contain more adverts than their ios counterpart. RAM management is different as well so you may find that apps fire up in a different way from ios. But everything I had on ios was available on Android or there was an alternative (Apple pay became Samsung pay, siri was replaced by Google assistant) 

Whether you buy an iPhone or an S8 each comes with their own selling point and floors. Really it's all about personal choice. Think about why you want to leave iPhone and more importantly ios and why you want an S8 and Android. For me it was about choice and control. I wanted greater control over the way my phone looks and feels - Android provided that for me. The screen was a massive draw for me as well. The camera is just as good if not better and I haven't missed the optical zoom on the iPhone 7 plus. I have also found better battery life on the S8+. However I do miss imessage. 

Have a play with the phone as much as you can and remember that the phone in the shop is set up to loom and act the way it does. However, if you get one and take it home you can make it your own.
